content: Diflunisal is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke compared to individuals who do not take NSAIDs. These cardiovascular events can occur without warning and may be fatal. The risk is higher in individuals who use NSAIDs for extended periods. Seek emergency medical attention immediately if you experience symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side of the body, or slurred speech. Diflunisal should not be taken immediately before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. Diflunisal and other NSAIDs can cause serious gastrointestinal complications, including ulcers, bleeding, or perforations in the stomach or intestines. These issues can occur at any time during treatment, often without warning, and may be fatal. The risk is higher in individuals who use NSAIDs long-term, are older, have poor overall health, or consume large amounts of alcohol. Notify your doctor if you are taking anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), aspirin, other NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), or oral steroids (e.g., prednisone, dexamethasone). Also, inform your doctor if you have a history of ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, or other bleeding disorders. If you experience symptoms such as stomach pain, heartburn, vomiting blood or material resembling coffee grounds, blood in the stool, or black, tarry stools, stop taking diflunisal and contact your doctor immediately. Your doctor will monitor your condition closely and may order tests to evaluate your response to diflunisal. It is important to communicate how you are feeling so that your doctor can adjust your dosage to minimize the risk of serious side effects. You will receive a Medication Guide from your doctor or pharmacist when starting diflunisal and with each prescription refill. Read this information carefully and ask any questions you may have. Additional information can be found on the FDA or manufacturer’s website. Diflunisal is prescribed to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness associated with osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It is also used to manage mild to moderate pain from other causes. Diflunisal works by inhibiting the production of substances in the body that cause pain, fever, and inflammation. This medication is available in tablet form and should be taken orally with water, milk, or food every 8-12 hours. Take it at the same times each day, following the instructions on your prescription label. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not split, chew, or crush the tablets. It may take several days or longer to experience the full benefits of diflunisal. Continue taking the medication as directed by your doctor. Before starting diflunisal, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, aspirin, other NSAIDs, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially those mentioned in the warning section. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication regimen or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have a history of asthma, nasal polyps, swelling in the extremities, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Diflunisal should not be taken during the last months of pregnancy. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking diflunisal. Do not take diflunisal if you suspect you have a viral infection, such as chickenpox or the flu, and do not give it to children with viral illnesses. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking diflunisal. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Diflunisal may cause side effects. Common side effects include vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, gas, headache, dizziness, ringing in the ears, and vision problems. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include upset stomach, extreme fatigue, unusual bleeding or bruising, itching, loss of appetite, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, rash, blisters, fever, chills, pale skin, rapid heartbeat, muscle or joint pain, unexplained weight gain, back pain, changes in urination, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, and difficulty swallowing or breathing. If you experience any of these, stop taking diflunisal and contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual side effects to your doctor or the FDA’s MedWatch program. Store diflunisal in its original container, tightly sealed, at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, consulting your pharmacist if needed. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call emergency services at 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include drowsiness, vomiting, upset stomach, diarrhea, reduced urination, rapid breathing, fast heartbeat, sweating, ringing in the ears, confusion, or loss of consciousness. Before undergoing any laboratory tests, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking diflunisal. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
